glosses: to bring in (to move something or someone inside something or on top of something)

examples.text: Ile paczek papierosów na dobę wwozili do Polski przemytnicy w pierwszym kwartale tego roku?

glosses: wioząc dostarczyć coś lub kogoś do wyżej położonego miejsca

examples.text: Kolejka linowa na Czantorię wwozi do 1800 turystów na godzinę.

glosses: To move something indoors, or into an area.

examples.text: Could you bring in the groceries?
The country brings in raw materials from overseas.
The causeways were laid as hard paths for heavily laden pack-animals bringing in wool from outlying hamlets and farms.
Unlike South Heath, where the tunnel segments are made on site, the ones used here are made off-site and brought in by road.

glosses: To introduce a new rule, law, or system of organisation.
To introduce, add or initiate a person or group of people to an organisation; to give (someone) a share or portion of something.

examples.text: I've brought him in on the plan.

glosses: To earn money for a company or for the family.

examples.text: BT shelled out almost £1bn for the Champions League over the same period, while the FA has just brought in around £820m over six seasons for the international rights to the FA Cup alone.

glosses: To return a verdict in a court of law.
